title: Phase 1 — Draft-Only Gmail Classifier for Straightforward Enquiries

sections.label: 1 · WATCH THE INBOX, IGNORE THE NOISE
sections.note: Newsletters, internal mail, automated notifications, results emails and spam never reach classification. The same message never gets processed twice, even if Gmail re-delivers it.

sections.label: 2 · CLASSIFY AND EXTRACT ONLY WHAT'S NEEDED
sections.note: The model reads the email and returns a category, a confidence score, and only the specific fields required: sender's first name, stated age, requested location, whether insurance is mentioned. Nothing else leaves this step.

sections.label: 3 · THE OUT-OF-SCOPE GATE
sections.note: This is the rule that matters most. An email that mixes a simple question with a test, price, clinical, or requisition question is sent to a human in full. No partial draft is ever written, even for the simple part.

sections.label: 4 · BUILD THE DRAFT FROM APPROVED CONTENT ONLY
sections.note: The wording comes from the approved Google Sheet, never from the model's own knowledge, and never from the internet. Staff can update a location, an opening time, or the approved wording without anyone touching the workflow.

sections.label: 5 · HUMAN REVIEW
sections.note: Unclear age, unclear location, mixed topics, or anything outside the three approved categories lands here labelled and untouched. Nothing is guessed at.

sections.label: 6 · LOG EVERY OUTCOME, ALERT ON FAILURE
sections.note: Every email gets one row, success or review, so accuracy can be audited from day one. A failed step anywhere alerts immediately instead of failing silently.

input_sample.subject: Opening hours + a quick test question
input_sample.body: Hi, what time does your Manchester clinic open on Saturdays? Also, do you test for ferritin there and roughly how much would that cost?

output_sample.straightforward_part_detected: Clinic location and opening hours — Manchester
output_sample.out_of_scope_part_detected: Specific test name (ferritin) plus a price request
